_provenance.also_not_covered: Presence, not emission. This gate proves a value still exists in a snapshot, not that any code path still emits it — so a value moved to an unread key within the same edition stays silent, the same limit the foreign gate has for dead code.
_provenance.commit_semantics: The tree whose SCANNER AND DATA together reproduce inventory_when_written. An earlier revision recorded the commit that happened to be HEAD when the regeneration script ran, which was the commit BEFORE the scanner change — so checking it out reproduced a different inventory and the field asserted something untrue (Sol, PR #56). Re-record this whenever the scanner or the counted shapes change, not only when the numbers move.
_provenance.covers: The DATA half of DF-16: article ids that reach an audit from packaged JSON rather than from an article= literal — read as spec["article"] or rule["trigger_article"], or resolved through ruleset.article(key) from a manifest registry. Before this gate, editing or deleting one moved neither citation gate nor the generated coverage document.
_provenance.does_not_cover: DF-16 stays OPEN for Python value flow: every citation whose article= expression is guarded while the value reaching it can change upstream — the 38 variable sites, the 10 Call/IfExp sites, and any f-string fed by an unguarded binding. NOT because those values are unresolvable: folding a name to its in-function assignment expression reaches 13 of 38, and most parameter sites have a same-module caller passing an f-string, so roughly 32 are reachable with one hop (Fable, PR #56). An earlier draft of this field claimed the values "arrive as function parameters and no static key can see them", on a measurement that folded only ast.Constant and resolved 1 of 38. Deferred on blast radius, not impossibility.
_provenance.rebaseline_reason: Re-baselined for the D-100 envelope review's edition-owned citation fix. Two hard-coded NECB 2020 literals were replaced by ruleset.article() lookups, so their literal counts drop to zero by design: 'Table 3.2.2.2.; 3.1.1.7.(4)' in envelope/prescriptive.py and the Note 'A-8.4.4.4.(1)' inside reference.py's thermal-mass citation. Article 3.1.1.7 keeps its number across editions but was restructured from eight sentences to four, so the enclosure credit moved 2020 (4) -> 2025 (3) and inclination moved 2020 (6) -> 2025 (4); the literal cited the wrong sentence on every 2025 run and never cited inclination at all. The thermal-mass Note moved A-8.4.4.4.(1) -> A-8.4.5.4.(1). Citations are not lost: they are now resolved per edition and BOTH clauses are emitted, which the static literal scanner cannot see.
_provenance.scope_rule: Edition snapshots own their own values; btap/codes/data/** is "shared". Scoping is load-bearing: removing an article from 2020 while 2025 gains the same one leaves both the repository total AND the global count of that value unchanged, so only the scope can fire.
_provenance.source: values of ['article', 'trigger_article'] keys, plus each manifest "articles" registry mapping, under btap/**/data/**/*.json

_provenance: Re-baselined 2026-10-08 on Sol's `137`, which is a NORMATIVE ruling and not a tidy-up. NECB 2020 does not contain Articles 8.4.1.5, 8.4.2.11 or 8.4.2.12, nor even Sentence 8.4.2.2.(6) — he verified it against the official NRC NECB 2020 second printing including the 2025-02-27 errata, citing Division B page 8-2 (Subsection 8.4.1 ends at Article 8.4.1.4), page 8-3 (8.4.2 starts at 8.4.2.1, and 8.4.2.2 has Sentences (1)-(5) only) and page 8-5 (8.4.2.10 is the last article of the subsection). The HBIX 2020-to-2025 Part 8 comparison labels all three NEW in 2025. So the packaged 2020 snapshot was right and our 2020 COVERAGE DATA was citing another edition's articles. There is no snapshot omission and no MCP defect to report. Three edits, exactly as ruled: the `8.4.1.5.` row is DELETED rather than renumbered, because 2020 has no one-for-one counterpart; the `8.4.2.2.(4)` row STAYS and only its "(see 8.4.2.11.)" pointer goes, because 2020's software-conformance requirement is in that sentence itself, which names ANSI/ASHRAE 140; and the `8.4.2.2.(6)` row is DELETED whole, with the exceptional-calculation route NOT mapped onto the Code's general alternative-solution framework, because Sol ruled they are not the same requirement. The 2025 claims and `necb_8_4_disposition.json` are untouched: all three provisions exist there. This is a LOSS of two citation sites and it is the correct loss — they cited articles that do not exist.

Re-baselined 2026-10-09: necb2025's `dx_staging.article` was `8.4.4.10.(8)`, an article NECB 2025 does not have — it renumbered Cooling Systems to 8.4.5.10 and the neighbouring `cooling_plant` was shifted while this one was missed. 2025 therefore loses `8.4.4.10.(8)` (1) and `8.4.5.10.(8)` rises 1 -> 2. necb2020 is UNCHANGED: 8.4.4.10.(8) is correct there. Nothing read the stale value — `_stage_multispeed_coil` takes its article as a parameter built from the edition prefix — so no audit, report or frozen baseline moved, and no re-freeze follows. Found while measuring the work to establish `editions` on the 97 unverified decisions; `TestDataCitationsAreValidForTheirEdition` is the gate that now refuses it, and the count gates beside it do NOT fire on this class because a wrong id can simply be recorded and then defended.
